title: What they said at the time

clips.q: And yet, Quibi is not succeeding. Likely for one of two reasons: because the idea itself wasn’t strong enough to justify a standalone streaming service or because of our timing.
clips.who: **Jeffrey Katzenberg and Meg Whitman**, open letter, Oct 21, 2020[^1]

clips.q: I attribute everything that has gone wrong to coronavirus. Everything. But we own it.
clips.who: **Jeffrey Katzenberg**, to the New York Times, May 11, 2020[^5]

clips.q: It turns out people have in-between moments at home. We don’t actually think it hurt us.
clips.who: **Meg Whitman**, on the pandemic, as reported from her CNBC interview of Apr 13, 2020[^6]

clips.q: People on Quibi have $100,000 a minute to make content. That doesn’t exist on other platforms.
The streamer that was doomed to fail before it launched has died
Most entrepreneurs just keep on going because they literally run out of money and we just didn’t think that was the right thing to do.
We’re pivoting from Quibi’s SVOD model to an ad-supported model, and this type of new, original content is not usually available for free.
clips.who: **Rob Holmes**, Roku vice-president of programming, to Variety, Jan 8, 2021[^16]
**Jeffrey Katzenberg**, asked by Deadline what was next, Oct 21, 2020[^2]
